CONCORDIA UNIVERSITY, "A HISTORY OF BURSARY AWARD WINNERS 1989-2006"
The A. Ross Seaman Leadership Development Fund, published 23 May 2007

Internet Archive identifier: 2007-05-23-a-ross-seaman-memorial-a-history-of-award-winners
Collection: rma-concordia-publications | 66,443 characters of OCR
Found 2026-09-07 by the accounted whole-corpus sweep of that collection under
p_479. Not previously in sources.json.

WHAT IT IS. A commemorative booklet Concordia printed eighteen months short of
the fund's twentieth year, reprinting the fund's memorial statement and then a
citation for every bursary winner from 1989 to 2006, most with a photograph.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE MEMORIAL STATEMENT, AS PRINTED HERE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  "We lost a community leader; educational innovator; consummate teacher and
  mentor with the passing of A. Ross Seaman on October 23, 1987. His death is a
  loss to countless people from the many places where he expended his energies
  and warmth to help others become the best they could be. Those who knew Ross
  best remember him for being on the leading edge of bringing the best possible
  resources to bear on the issues that engaged his energy; camping and
  leadership training, recreation leadership and community organization,
  particularly when it related to adolescent life, and latterly, when it related
  to an aging population. One colleague referred to him as A CHEERLEADER FOR THE
  HUMAN RACE and this special quality which he possessed and shared so
  generously, warrants remembrance on our part.

  One of Ross's philosophies was to 'PASS IT ON' whenever he was on the
  receiving end of something meaningful and important to him. The A. Ross Seaman
  Leadership Development Fund will enable students in a variety of leadership
  areas to pursue studies and/or experiences that will further their own
  leadership potential and skills. In this way Ross will remain with us, and his
  impact on our own growth and development will continue to be felt by those who
  follow in his footsteps."

THIS IS A THIRD WITNESS TO A TEXT THE WIKI HOLDS FROM ONE SOURCE. Canadian
Camping Magazine's fund notice of Winter 1988 and Concordia's Applied Human
Sciences department both carry versions of it, and wiki/people/a-ross-seaman.md
quotes them. Three small textual variants are worth recording rather than
smoothing:

  - "a cheerleader FOR the human race" here; the wiki has "a cheerleader OF the
    human race" from the Canadian Camping notice.
  - "consummate teacher AND MENTOR" here; "consummate teacher" alone in the
    Concordia University Magazine obituary of January 1988.
  - The fund is "the A. Ross Seaman Leadership Development Fund" here and in the
    magazine; the wiki's article and Concordia's own scholarship listing call it
    the A. Ross Seaman MEMORIAL Leadership Development Fund. Both names are in
    use by the university itself.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT THE CITATIONS SHOW, AND WHY IT MATTERS TO THIS WIKI
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

"Kanawana" occurs TWENTY-SEVEN times in the booklet, across the citations of
1989 to 2006. The camp is by a wide margin the most frequently named single
institution in the winners' backgrounds after Concordia itself and the YMCA
generally. The roles named in those citations include camper,
counsellor-in-training, junior counsellor, senior counsellor, nature specialist,
senior camp programme lead, and off-season volunteer.

THE INSTITUTIONAL FINDING IS THAT KANAWANA WAS A STANDING FEEDER COMMUNITY FOR
THE FUND ACROSS NEARLY TWO DECADES. A memorial fund set up in Montreal in
November 1987 by representatives of Concordia, Dawson College, the YMCA and Camp
Kanawana went on, year after year, to award its bursary to people whose
leadership had been formed at that camp. The circuit Seaman himself ran -- camp
into college into the profession -- was still running twenty years after his
death, under his name.

Two particular things:

1. A DIRECT TESTIMONY ABOUT SEAMAN AS A MENTOR, from a winner of the Applied
   Human Sciences Human Relations Award: she "caught the 'leadership bug' early
   in her professional career AS A CAMP NURSE, UNDER THE MENTORSHIP OF ROSS
   SEAMAN." This project holds a great deal about what Seaman did and very
   little from anyone he taught. It also puts a camp nurse in his orbit, a role
   the wiki has almost nothing on.

2. A DATED INSTANCE OF THE CAPITAINE ROLE. One citation records a man who came
   to Kanawana in the summer of 1992 as a camper and rose through
   counsellor-in-training and junior counsellor to senior counsellor, and was
   "selected as the 'CAPITAINE' of the Voyageurs for the annual summer-ending
   Lumbermen and Voyageurs games." wiki/traditions/lv-games.md has a section on
   the Capitaine role; this is an outside document attesting it, with a named
   holder and a decade.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN INTO THE WIKI, AND WHY -- READ THIS BEFORE
CONCLUDING THE SOURCE IS THIN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The booklet names every winner, 1989 through 2006, and describes each one's
character, career and camp service in a paragraph. Those people are living
private individuals, most of them students at the time, the youngest of them
awarded within twenty years of this reading. CLAUDE.md's standing instruction is
to extract institutional facts, historical information and information about
public figures, and not personal information about living private individuals.

SO THE ROSTER IS NOT REPRODUCED IN THE WIKI, AND THIS RECORD EXISTS SO THAT A
LATER PASS CAN TELL THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A SOURCE THAT SAYS NOTHING AND A
DECISION NOT TO WRITE SOMETHING DOWN. The names are in the booklet at the
Internet Archive identifier above; the Kanawana-connected citations are at OCR
lines 69-72, 175, 415, 545, 664, 949-955, 1037, 1067-1072, 1107-1111, 1122-1125
and 1191-1199. Registered as r_0006 in kb/restricted/register.jsonl. Nothing is
being protected from disclosure that the university has not itself published;
what is being avoided is this wiki assembling a searchable biography of a
private person out of an honour roll.

The two individual details written up above -- the camp nurse's testimony about
Seaman, and the Capitaine selection -- are kept because their subject is Seaman
and a camp tradition respectively, and both are written without the person's
name.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NULL RESULTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
"Otoreke" 0, "Perrot" 0, "Voyageurs de la" 0 (the one Voyageurs occurrence is
the L&V games team).

"VANKLEEK" IS NOT 0. It occurs once, and the first draft of this cache said
zero -- written from expectation rather than from the grep, and caught by
running the counts before saving. The occurrence is a winner's citation: "Good
student, good marks, leading basketball scorer in VANKLEEK HILL COLLEGIATE.
Volunteered as a coach in minor hockey, basketball & soccer in his community."

That is worth having on its own. wiki/people/a-ross-seaman.md records that five
organizations honour Seaman through scholarships -- Dawson, Concordia, Kamp
Kanawana, the YMCA and Vankleek Hill Collegiate -- which reads as five separate
awards. Here the CONCORDIA fund is itself awarding its bursary to a boy from
Seaman's home-town high school, some hundred kilometres away in eastern Ontario.
The Vankleek Hill connection is not only a separate memorial in his home town;
it runs through the Montreal fund as well.

It does NOT bear on the outstanding question of Seaman's birth record. Nothing
here gives a date, a family name, or a parish.
